original.reason: The proof contains an unjustified/false divisibility statement when i-2j may be negative, and it does not properly establish the sufficient direction needed to conclude that n is a sum of two integer squares.

judgment.reason: It correctly clears denominators, proves even valuations for primes congruent to 3 mod 4, and applies the sum-of-two-squares theorem.
It correctly derives even exponents for all primes congruent to 3 mod 4 after clearing denominators, then invokes the standard characterization.
The valuation argument is correct and the zero case is explicitly addressed; the concluding application of the sum-of-two-squares theorem is valid.

Its proof of the key claim has a gap: ruling out that p divides exactly one of U,V does not rule out p dividing neither. The required quadratic-residue argument for the neither-divisible case is omitted.
